cells.tense: You give and receive evenly right now, and wanting something real and treating people fairly are feeding each other.
cells.ask: Let one person do something for you today without balancing it, then notice what it does to what you aim at next.
cells.core:
You want something real, and the way you give and take has stopped fighting it. The exchange is clean — no score kept under the table. That matters here, because wanting something in this part of life runs on resonance: you keep moving toward what you actually want when nobody owes anybody anything.
The bend, if there is one, is small. The same fairness that keeps you from over-giving also keeps you from letting people close enough to see why you gave. This balance holds up better in plain sight than as bookkeeping you don't show. The ask is yours, not a rule: receive something today without paying it back, and watch what that does to what you reach for next.
cells.sheetLine: You give and take evenly, and you still know what you want.
cells.verb: giving and receiving in plain balance
cells.place: the draw toward what you actually want

cells.tense: You will be working out how the exchange is going to come out fair before you let it start.
cells.ask: Give one thing today without tracking what comes back, and see whether the exchange really collapses.
cells.core:
You're ahead of the moment, already balancing a ledger nobody opened. Before a gift is given you've worked out what it will cost and what it will owe. Not stinginess — the same care that makes your generosity land, running hot. You're trying to guarantee fairness in advance, and fairness doesn't survive being guaranteed.
What you actually want gets dim when you're managing the exchange. Wanting needs some openness in order to receive anything at all, and calculation closes that door. Sit with the aim without forcing it through a balance sheet. Give once today without tracking the return, and let the answer — comes back or doesn't — be information, not a verdict on you.
cells.sheetLine: You're balancing a ledger nobody asked you to keep.
cells.verb: giving and receiving in plain balance
cells.place: the draw toward what you actually want

cells.tense: You gave or asked and the exchange did not come out even, and you are still in that doorway.
cells.ask: Ask one person for something small and specific, and let them answer without smoothing it over.
cells.core:
Something in you stopped trusting the exchange. You hold back before you even notice you're doing it, so what you want feels thin — you can still name what you're drawn to, but the path to it looks like it runs through other people, which is where it gets complicated.
That's the bend. Not that you don't want what you want, but that you've stopped expecting anyone to meet you on the way there. The exchange hasn't gone anywhere. Asking is what stopped. One specific request today, small enough to survive any answer, is a way to test whether the door really is still closed — and to notice what moves when you step out of the frame.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking, and now what you want looks like it runs through other people.

cells.tense: You are already running a fair exchange with the people around you and you talk about it like you are only watching it happen.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one fair thing you did was yours, then leave it alone.
cells.core:
You give and take in a way people feel. There's a fairness in how you handle things that doesn't announce itself, and you describe it as luck, mood, or just how things went. The exchange keeps running. You haven't claimed it. That gap isn't modesty — it's a pen set down at a desk you're still sitting at, on a page still being filled.
What you want in this part of life is recognized, not assigned, which means whoever notices it is the one who gets to hold it. The work underneath is to hold the truth of one thing you did before you explain it away, to anyone including yourself. Say it plainly once, without hedging, and see how much clearer the next thing you reach for becomes.
cells.sheetLine: The exchange is already running. You just haven't owned it.

cells.place: the draw toward what you actually want

The ask survives being wrong because it moves toward the medicine rather than fixing the card: one act of exact reciprocity can be done even if the read is off. The line that serves me more than them is 'the harvest is already shared' — it flatters the mechanism and would let me off the hook of actually naming where the bend is.
